### Problem Summary

When parsing a timestamp string like `"01-01-2013T00:00:00.000000000+0000"`, the `dateutil` parser may not correctly interpret the trailing zeros in the fractional seconds part. This results in `pandas` inferring a lower resolution (e.g., `"s"` for seconds) than intended, even though the string contains more precise time information (e.g., nanoseconds).

### Root Cause

The `dateutil` parser (used by `pandas` for string parsing) has logic that attempts to reduce the resolution of the timestamp if the fractional part has trailing zeros. For example, if the microsecond part is `0`, it reduces the resolution to seconds. If the microsecond part is a multiple of `1000`, it reduces it to milliseconds. This logic can cause `pandas` to incorrectly infer the unit as `"s"` instead of `"ns"` or `"us"`.
